paragraphs: Leo and Lily made a poster for Star Night. "Our school is one century old this year," said Teacher Kim. All the children wanted to look at the stars together. It was a big night for the school. Leo drew a big yellow moon, and Lily wrote the words. Leo and Lily put the poster on the wall of the school hall.

This is what the poster said. "SCHOOL STAR NIGHT!" "Our school is one century old, so come and look at the stars with us." "Day: Friday." "Time: seven o'clock until nine o'clock, not until midnight!" "Place: the school field. If it rains, we use the hall." "A big screen shows old photos of our school." "Visit the star table, and make a wish on a paper star." "Can you find the moon and three stars?" "Please bring a mat and a bottle of water." "Keep your star in your pocket."

Leo laughed when he read the word midnight. "Can we stay until midnight?" he asked. "No, nine o'clock is good for everyone," said Teacher Kim. "The younger children must sleep early." "Also, the stars look best at eight o'clock," she said. Lily smiled and looked at the poster again. "It is a good poster," she said.

That evening, Lily wrote an email to Grace. "Dear Grace, this is Lily. Our school has a Star Night on Friday. It is on the school field from seven o'clock until nine o'clock. If it rains, we go to the hall. A big screen shows old photos of the school. Some photos are as old as the school. Do you like to look at the stars in Singapore? We have a hundred paper stars for the wishes. Please make a wish for us in Singapore. Your friend, Lily" Lily sent the email, and then she went to bed.
